props.title: Labyrinth
props.initialSlug: Jim Henson fantasy combining puppetry and practical effects

sections.content: Labyrinth (1986) stands as Jim Henson's dark fantasy masterpiece, blending practical puppetry with early CGI in ways that still captivate. The film pairs David Bowie's magnetic Goblin King with Jennifer Connelly's coming-of-age journey, creating a spiritual successor to The Dark Crystal (1982). Henson's creature workshop outdid themselves - the hands that made The Muppets crafted an entirely new mythology of goblins, helping hands, and the scene-stealing Hoggle. Like The NeverEnding Story (1984) and Return to Oz (1985), it embraces darker children's fantasy that trusts young audiences with complex themes.

sections.content: Bowie's soundtrack elevates Labyrinth beyond typical fantasy fare. "Magic Dance" and "As the World Falls Down" aren't just songs - they're story beats that drive the narrative. This marriage of music and fantasy storytelling influenced later works like Moulin Rouge! (2001) and Into the Woods (2014). The ballroom scene in particular, with its masked dancers and shattered mirrors, became a template for fantasy-musical sequences.

The film's practical effects deserve special attention. While contemporaries like Legend (1985) and The Princess Bride (1987) used similar techniques, Labyrinth pushed boundaries with its combination of forced perspective, puppetry, and early computer graphics. The Escher-inspired final confrontation remains a masterclass in practical effects storytelling that later CGI-heavy films like Alice in Wonderland (2010) attempted to recreate digitally. sections.content: Labyrinth's influence extends far beyond fantasy films. Its themes of female empowerment and coming-of-age resonate in works like Coraline (2009) and Pan's Labyrinth (2006). The practical effects renaissance in films like The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance (2019) owes much to Labyrinth's pioneering work. Even modern fantasy series like The Witcher (2019) echo its perfect balance of whimsy and darkness.
